analysis: The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md (+5 lines at the top, patch hunk @@ -1,4 +1,9 @@). It adds an 'Unreleased - KV admission estimates' section with two bullets. (1) Ordinary engine concurrency is reduced when fixed recurrent/MTP workspace would consume the KV grant. Heartbeats and local admission use the same memory-limited width. Load, activation and minimum-KV safeguards are stated as not lowered. (2) Cold-model KV cost is estimated from fresh native reports for the same artifact and verified runtime, replacing the generic bytes-per-token fallback. Live slot budgets stay authoritative, missing evidence keeps the fallback, and provider memory checks still decide fit. The PR contains documentation only, with no source, config, or threat-model YAML changes. No code was supplied, so the claims cannot be checked against implementation. Relevant threats if the underlying code lands elsewhere: provider-reported native KV reports are untrusted input from adversarial providers (ADV-001) over TB-002. A malicious provider could under-report KV cost to attract more admission or over-report it to shed load. The changelog says live slot budgets remain authoritative and the provider's own memory checks decide, so the admission impact is bounded to scheduling and availability. It does not alter attestation, encryption, authorization, or billing. The next pass should confirm that any accompanying coordinator or provider code (not in this batch) binds the reports to the verified artifact and runtime identity. It should also confirm that reports are freshness-bounded and clamped, and that heartbeat-reported concurrency cannot exceed coordinator-side caps. No security regression is evident from the supplied content.
